IR.rationale: A rising belly-minus-policy spread with no matching rise in front-end bill rates means term premium is being rebuilt without policy tightening. Term-premium predictability (Fama-Bliss, Cochrane-Piazzesi) says this should raise subsequent excess bond returns.

B.rationale: Stable or narrowing high-grade spreads together with strong high-yield returns describe easy credit conditions. That state shifts demand between duration and credit and so bears on investment-grade and Treasury returns.

V.rationale: Elevated oil volatility often accompanies growth and disinflation scares. These push investors toward safe duration and lower expected policy rates.

AP.rationale: Equity factor returns carry little stable predictive information for the next-period level of government bond returns beyond what credit and volatility already capture.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to subsequent Treasury returns.

FX.rationale: A strengthening dollar tightens global financial conditions and dampens imported inflation. Both support lower yields and positive bond returns.

COM.rationale: Falling oil prices lower inflation expectations and breakevens, which feeds into lower nominal yields.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions raise flight-to-quality demand and expectations of accommodative policy, both of which favour government bonds.

ENDG.rationale: Bond returns show time-series momentum at medium horizons and some short-horizon reversal. The index's own recent return state is therefore informative, and the model sets the sign.

IR.rationale: Sharp curve steepening signals term-premium or inflation-risk repricing at the long end. Such episodes cluster with elevated rate volatility.

B.rationale: Weak high-yield returns signal credit stress. That brings flight-to-quality flows and larger subsequent swings in Treasury yields.

V.rationale: Gold volatility reflects uncertainty about real rates, inflation and the dollar, which is closely tied to future bond-market volatility.

AP.rationale: Equity sell-offs trigger safe-haven reallocations and repricing of policy expectations, raising subsequent bond volatility.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no direct mechanism tying them to future rate volatility.

FX.rationale: Sharp dollar appreciation tightens global funding conditions and is often linked to shifts in Fed expectations. This raises uncertainty about yields.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity declines feed disinflation and growth scares that reprice the rate path, adding to bond volatility.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions are associated with higher future volatility across asset classes, including rates, beyond what own-volatility persistence captures.

ENDG.rationale: Realised bond variance is persistent but mean-reverting. Its own recent level indicates whether future variance will exceed what persistence alone implies.

IR.rationale: A bear-steepening state, with long and intermediate yields rising relative to the policy rate, marks term-premium repricing. Such repricing tends to extend into large duration losses.

B.rationale: Weak EM sovereign returns signal an unwinding of global reach-for-yield positions. That can coincide with rising US yields and sell-offs in dollar duration.

V.rationale: High gold volatility signals uncertainty about real rates and inflation, which raises the chance of a sharp bond sell-off.

AP.rationale: Value outperformance, led by financials and cyclicals, reflects reflation and rising-yield expectations. That state precedes bond losses.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors offer no clear mechanism for the left tail of bond returns.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar points to reflation and reduced foreign demand for Treasuries. Both raise the risk of large yield increases.

COM.rationale: Oil price surges lift inflation expectations and nominal yields, raising the chance of large bond losses.

MC.rationale: Rising breakeven inflation feeds directly into nominal yields and inflation-risk premia. This is a main driver of bond sell-offs.

ENDG.rationale: Recent weak bond returns indicate an ongoing sell-off that can continue through momentum or deleveraging, or reverse; the model sets which.

IR.rationale: Falling bill rates signal flight to safety or expectations of policy easing, which precede strong duration rallies.

B.rationale: Movements in high-grade spreads relative to Treasuries capture the safe-asset premium. Their state is informative about subsequent large rallies in government and investment-grade bonds.

V.rationale: Commodity-driven uncertainty spikes accompany growth and disinflation scares that produce large bond rallies.

AP.rationale: Equity factor returns add little reliable information on the right tail of bond returns beyond the volatility and financial-conditions groups.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no clear mechanism for large bond gains.

FX.rationale: Currency moves relate to bond rallies mainly through channels already captured by financial conditions and volatility.

COM.rationale: Commodity returns' information on large bond gains is largely captured by the volatility and inflation-expectation factors.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions raise the probability of flight-to-quality episodes and policy easing that generate large Treasury gains.

ENDG.rationale: Strong recent bond returns indicate a rally in progress, which may extend through momentum or mean-revert; the model sets the direction.
